chapters.title: Chapter 693: Divine Favor Gauge
paragraphs: [Congratulations, Broken, for your ascension to a new role! You have received the following new titles and skills:]
[You have received a new title: Consort of Dissidia's Radiance.]
[This title reflects your role as a protective and inspiring presence through your union with Alora Rogwyn.]
[Effect: Allies within a 10-meter radius receive 5% damage reduction.]
[You have received a new title: Vowkeeper of Dissidia's Accord.]
[This title represents the strength of your Sacred Bond with Alora Rogwyn and your shared determination to protect the kingdom.]
[You have received a new skill: Sacred Bond Resilience (Passive).]
[Effect: You and Alora take 10% less damage when fighting together. Additionally, healing received by both is boosted by 20%.]
[You have received a new title: Champion of Dissidia's Sacred Flame.]
[This title ties your power to the divine energies invoked during the Sacred Bond ceremony.]
[Effect: Attacks have a 10% chance to deal an additional 15% fire damage over three seconds. Fire damage taken is reduced by 10%.]
[You have received a new title: Blade of Dissidia's Throne.]
[This title signifies your prowess as the kingdom's combat champion, excelling in melee combat.]
[Effect: You have unlocked the skill Thronebreaker's Edge (Passive). Melee attacks deal 5% more damage to heavily armored enemies.]
[You have received a new title: Pillar of Dissidia's Shining Throne.]
[This title reflects your growing influence and ability to unify allies under Dissidia's banner.]
[Effect: Allied NPCs and party members gain +10% HP and +5% attack power while within Dissidia's borders.]
[You have received a new title: Keeper of Dissidia's Radiant Bond.]
[This title highlights your status as Alora's consort and a symbol of unity across the kingdom.]
[Effect: All NPCs in Dissidia start with +10% base affinity toward you. Diplomatic negotiations have a 5% higher success rate.]
[You have received a new title: Guardian of Dissidia's Legacy.]

[This title signifies your role as a preserver of Dissidia's heritage and resources.] [Effect: All items crafted have a 5% chance to gain an additional random enhancement.] Broken was bombarded with a barrage of notifications-achievement rewards, titles, and new skills-following his marriage to Princess Alora. However, he skimmed through them quickly, determining that none of the updates required his immediate attention.

There wasn't a single active skill he could utilize right away. The only clear takeaways were that he needed to fight alongside Princess Alora to fully optimize their combined potential, and that they would both receive a boost when fighting within the boundaries of the Dissidia Kingdom.
His attention, however, was soon drawn to the ring Princess Alora had given him in exchange for the Ring of Unlimited Skillz he had handed over to her.

The reason he'd given her that particular ring was simple: it was the only one he could spare. The others were either bound to him or unsuitable-like the ring he'd obtained after killing Melliandra, an item he would never consider for something as sacred as a wedding.
Admittedly, in less dire circumstances, he might have taken the time to choose a more fitting wedding ring. But now, his thoughts turned to the one Alora had placed on his finger.
[Ring of Relentless Casting]
[Grade: Unique]
[Durability: 87/100]
[Weight: 12]
[This ring channels the essence of untiring resolve, empowering its wearer to cast without hesitation and ensuring their magic flows uninterrupted.]
[Skills:]
[Grants a 5% chance to reset the cooldown of any activated skill, allowing immediate reuse.] [Reduces all skill cooldowns by 10%.]
[User Restriction: 500 Intelligence]
It was a Unique-grade ring with a skill... wait, a 5% chance to reset cooldowns?!
Damn! Isn't that chance ridiculously high for a Unique-grade ring?
As if that wasn't enough, it also provided a 10% cooldown reduction.
Compared to the ring he had given to Alora-which granted a 5% chance to cast a skill without consuming mana―this one seemed just as extraordinary. Perhaps even more so.
Resetting cooldowns wasn't just useful; it was outright overpowered.
"Princess, are you sure you didn't accidentally give me the wrong ring?" he asked, glancing at her.
"No Princess."
"Alora..."
"Yes, I'm sure," she said. "You can use it. I'm sure it'll be very useful for you."
There was no time for further discussion. They quickly climbed back onto Polly, who launched into the air with powerful wings, Frostedge following closely behind.
Even as they soared through the sky, his thoughts kept returning to one intriguing detail-a skill tied to the marriage itself, embedded within The Unbreakable Heart Ring.
He had skimmed over the notifications earlier, too preoccupied with the urgency of the moment.
Deciding it couldn't wait any longer, he summoned the notifications again. The familiar window materialized before him.
[A strong compatibility has been identified between the partner's innate traits and the ring's
characteristics.]
[Upgrading the ability grade...]
[Ability duplication successful!]
[Congratulations! You have unlocked a new skill.]
[Summon Golden Paragon (Conditional Active Skill)]
"Golden Paragon?"
Broken froze for a moment, the name alone enough to pique his curiosity. Without wasting any time, he quickly opened the details of the skill to see what it entailed.
[Summon Golden Paragon (Conditional Active Skill)]

[Unleash the ultimate celestial guardian-Golden Paragon, a divine avatar that embodies might and grace. The Golden Paragon is an extension of the summoner's will, amplifying their power and fighting with blinding radiance.]
[Summon Mechanic:]
[The Golden Paragon remains active as long as the summoner sustains it through the Divine
Favor Gauge.]
[The Divine Favor Gauge starts at 100% and drains at a rate of 5% per second. Actions refill the
gauge:]
[- Dealing damage: Restores 1% per attack.]
[- Healing allies: Restores 2% per action.]
[- Killing enemies: Restores 10% per kill.]
[Skill Effects:]

The skill was undeniably unique, with an exceptionally detailed description that covered everything—from its summoning mechanics and effects to the abilities of the summoned entity and a complex penalty system.

But Broken only managed to skim through the top section. It was clear that this wasn't a skill he could simply activate without a deeper understanding. If he misunderstood its intricacies, he might fail to utilize it to its full potential-or worse, end up wasting it entirely.
"Divine Favor Gauge?"
So, the summon would persist as long as he could keep the Divine Favor Gauge from depleting? That sounded... absurdly overpowered.

Under normal conditions, the summon would vanish after just 20 seconds. But with the ability to restore 1% per attack, 2% per heal, and a massive 10% for killing enemies, the gauge could potentially remain full.
As long as there were enemies to fight, allies to heal, and weaker foes to kill, this skill could theoretically last indefinitely.

Broken skimmed through the full details of the skill. After a moment of consideration, he decided there was no immediate need to activate it- at least not yet. Given their current circumstances, it was better to hold off.
For now, there was no time to spare.
But if this skill was truly as extraordinary as it seemed, Alora should know something about it.
Perhaps she could explain its significance and help him understand its proper use.
"Alora?" he called over his shoulder.
"Yes, Broken?" she responded.
"Do you know anything about Golden Paragon?"
This skill had clearly originated from her, but a question burned in his mind-why had he never seen her use it before?
"Y-yes..." she replied hesitantly. "But... how do you know about it, Broken?"

chapters.title: Chapter 694: Glacier Fang
paragraphs: "Do you know anything about Golden Paragon?" Broken asked Alora.
"Y-yes..." she replied hesitantly. "How do you know about it, Broken?"
"I gained access to the skill after marrying you," he explained.
"Oh, how?"
"How?"
"No..." Alora appeared confused. "Only the King is supposed to have access to Golden Paragon.
It's a skill passed down exclusively to the heirs of the throne."
"Wouldn't that mean you should also have access to Golden Paragon?"
"No... I don't think so, I don't know..." she said.
"You don't know? You can't activate the skill?"
"Yes, I don't know how to summon the Golden Paragon," she admitted.
"That's... confusing. Then why do I have it?"
"The Golden Paragon can only belong to one person at a time, Broken. Doesn't that mean... you've inherited the Avatar?"

"No," Broken replied firmly. "The system clearly stated that the skill was copied to me. That means you should still have access to it, especially since I only got it through marrying you- from the ring."
Alora fell silent.
"Don't worry," Broken said gently. "We can figure it out later. Let's focus on what's in front of us for now."
This raised a significant question. Broken was certain Alora should have access to the skill, but perhaps the conditions for her to activate it were different from his own.
Like how Elaine could only transform into Eternal Flame under the full moon, while I can activate it anytime as long as there's moonlight.

Shaking the thought aside for now, Broken refocused on the battlefield ahead. He knew the demons' numbers were overwhelming, and many were already wounded. Soon, there would be countless monsters eliminated, and his plan promised to deal massive damage.
But there was a major issue.
The experience points.
If he didn't act, all that valuable experience would go to waste. He wouldn't be able to utilize it on his own. To avoid this, he needed to invite someone to his party and share the rewards. But who?
Booba?
No, not him. At his current level, he'd benefit more from the stat points earned through fighting higher-leveled enemies directly. He wasn't urgent.
Elincia? Livelywood? No, that wouldn't work either-Livelywood was already defeated. Lily?
Bloom's level was still low, but she didn't urgently need the experience points right now. As he ran through the names in his mind, he finally remembered someone-his sister's friend: SexyGrill.

Yes. If he shared the experience points with her, he'd benefit later when they were in the same party. Her Divine Champion skill would kick in, granting him level increases based on the difference between their levels.
Without wasting another moment, Broken sent a party invitation to SexyGrill.
[SexyGrill]: "Broken... you finally showed up... I was starting to lose hope... Hua... : cry:"
[Broken]: "I'm about to shower you with a ton of experience points."
[SexyGrill]: "Alright! You've got perfect timing!"

Polly flew to a height where he could see the battlefield stretch out in every direction. From this vantage point, he prepared to unleash devastation using three of his most trusted weapons: the Bedrock Breaker Pickaxe, the Wavebreaker Spear, and the Gravestone Greatsword. There was also one more-a blade belonging to Frostedge.

He could've borrowed the Legendary-grade sword that belonged to... cough... his wife. But unfortunately, her sword was heavily focused on single-target damage, making it less than ideal for a combination attack with the Golden Bow of Artemis.
Frostedge soon joined him, standing beside him atop his own sword.
The meteor had nearly emerged halfway through the massive portal. It would soon free itself entirely and begin its deadly descent toward the ground.
"Broken, take my sword," Frostedge said suddenly.
Broken narrowed his eyes, looking at him. "How are you going to fly down below without your sword?"
"Don't worry," he replied. "And let me cast a buff for you before I go."
"Sure," he nodded.

Frostedge moved his fingers precisely, and a magic circle appeared above Broken's head. The glowing ring radiated a brilliant white and icy blue light, sending a cascade of energy down to envelop him entirely.
[You have received the buff: Frostbound Ascension.]

[For 60 seconds, all your attacks and skills deal an additional 50% Ice Elemental Damage. Skills with existing elemental effects gain bonus Ice Damage on top of their original effects. AoE abilities leave frost-covered ground that slows enemies by 30% for 5 seconds, and status effects have a 25% chance to freeze targets for 2 seconds.]
Oh damn. That's incredible!
Frostedge smiled and gave him a graceful bow. "Good luck."
Then, without warning, he tipped backward, letting himself fall freely through the air.
"Frostedge!" Broken shouted, alarmed.
No! He wouldn't do something reckless, would he? He had to be fine-there was no way someone like him would act carelessly.
As he watched in shock, Frostedge's sword flew toward him. He instinctively reached out and grabbed it.
[Legendary - Glacier Fang]
Oh, damn!
A Legendary-grade sword dropped from a monster? Just what kind of creature did he slay to obtain something like this?
[Alora's Fierce Empowerment (Conditional Active Skill) activated.]
With this, every skill Broken cast would function as if it were five levels higher than its original state.

He steadied himself, starting with the Bedrock Breaker Pickaxe. He could only use Sniper's Focus and Explosive Arrow once, but he held onto the hope that the new ring's skill might trigger and reset one of them.
Taking a deep breath, he aimed and prepared to unleash his power.
[Explosive Arrow (Active Skill) Lv. 10 activated.]
The ring's reset effect didn't trigger!
Damn!

Frostedge plummeted freely toward the ground, his figure cutting through the air with incredible speed. At the same time, Broken was in position, preparing to unleash his arsenal one by one toward the battlefield below.
No one noticed Frostedge's descent at first-until he neared the ground. With a swift motion, he slammed his hand toward the air. A massive glacier erupted instantly, towering into the air.
Gasps of shock echoed across the battlefield as those nearby turned to witness the spectacle.

With precise agility, Frostedge used the rising glacier as a ramp, falling himself onto the slope. He slid down effortlessly, his speed accelerating as the icy structure continued to grow beneath him, extending toward the demons.
The momentum was devastating. Frostedge carved through the battlefield, barreling into the horde of demons with a barrage of ice, sending them flying or pinning them beneath the encroaching frost.
"Frostedge?" someone shouted in disbelief.
"Frostedge has arrived!"
"Frostedge is here to help us!"

Right after Frostedge's icy onslaught, a series of explosions, tremors, and massive strikes rained down on all four gates simultaneously. The chaotic spectacle left no doubt-Broken had arrived on the battlefield.

Thanks to Frostedge's buff, Broken was delivering monumental damage with each attack. Notifications flooded his vision as countless demons fell to his devastating strikes. Finally, he disabled the notifications to stay focused, but it was clear-hundreds of demons had been obliterated by his four powerful shots.

[Broken]: "Only 3 levels?"
[SexyGrill]: "Sigh, I can see why someone passively gaining levels might say that."
[SexyGrill]: "It's because most of the demons weren't in full health, and Frostedge
contributed to the kills too."
Broken nodded to himself, already preparing for the next move on his list.
[Astral Aegis of Unity (One-Time Use)]
A ridiculously expensive item, capable of being used only once. This would have to count.

chapters.title: Chapter 695: Dome of Aetherial Unity
paragraphs: Broken activated every protective and defensive skill at his disposal, leaving nothing to chance. With his Invincible Paragon Set equipped, he brought each ability online.
[Blessing of Health (Active Skill) Lv. 6 activated.]
[Invincible Shields (Active Skill) activated.]
[Earth Skin (Active Skill) activated.]
[Earth Elemental Protection (Active Skill) activated.]
[Miner's Fortitude (Conditional Passive Skill) Lv. 3 activated.]
[Dome of Aetherial Unity (Active) activated.]

The miniature shield-shaped device he held began to hover above them, spinning rapidly. It projected a series of interlocking hexagonal shields that expanded outward, glowing gold as they connected and enveloped the entire city and the battlefield beyond.
At the same time, a massive meteor-blazing like a fragment of the sun-descended from the heavens. The ground shook violently and the temperature soared as the meteor neared impact.
Alora wrapped her arms around Broken from behind and resting her head gently against his back. "We can get through this," she whispered.
"Yes, we can!" Broken replied firmly.
He braced himself, unsure of just how devastating the impact would be.
[Nature's Herald (Active Skill) Lv. 2 activated.]

Broken summoned the Elder Dragon Tree, a majestic creature of vines, bark, and verdant energy. The dragon coiled through the air near him, releasing a shimmering cloud of pollen that washed over both him and Alora, providing them with additional reinforcement.
The meteor loomed ever closer.

Alora adjusted her stance slightly on Polly's back, drawing her Legendary-grade sword. As she held it aloft, an aura of earth energy began to swirl around them. Giant blocks of stone and hardened earth erupted from the thin air, rising rapidly to form protective layers that encased them from all directions.
The final moment was upon them.
The meteor, a fiery behemoth of destruction, slammed into the golden hexagonal barrier with a deafening roar.

For a moment, it seemed the barrier would hold-but then the blaze intensified. Flames, hotter than anything Broken had ever felt, surged outward in a torrent of fury. The hexagonal shield buckled under the pressure, cracks forming as the meteor's immense force bore down relentlessly.
BOOM!
The shield trembled but held, bending under the meteor's destructive force. Yet, the firestorm from the impact roared past its edges, tearing into every protection skill Broken had activated.
Broken gritted his teeth, his body straining against the meteor's relentless power. Beside him, the Elder Dragon Tree coiled protectively.
But the situation worsened quickly as his protective skills began to break, faltering under the intense heat and pressure.
His massive health pool was depleting rapidly, only to be partially replenished by the Elder Dragon Tree's healing abilities.
This isn't enough!
[Awaken the Nature Goddess (Active Skill) activated.]
A radiant, ethereal figure of Gaia emerged beside them.
[Nature Healing (Active Skill) activated.]
Broken felt the change instantly. The constant assault on his health stabilized, his wounds mending faster than the flames could burn him. But it was still a brutal battle of attrition.
Alora continued casting protective shields around them, layer after layer.
"I'm okay," she said, sensing his concern. "The damage I'm taking isn't as severe as what you're enduring, Broken."
He nodded but clenched his jaw. They couldn't hold out like this forever-not just the two of them.
The meteor's fury wasn't letting up, and every second that passed drained their resources further.
"We need reinforcements!"
Frostedge shot upward from below, moving with incredible speed. Standing atop his sword, he began casting spells. In moments, massive ice shards formed around them, encasing the group.

The shards absorbed the relentless heat and impact from the meteor, but each one shattered almost as quickly as it formed, forcing Frostedge to continuously regenerate the barriers. The three of them-Broken, Alora, and Frostedge-were locked in a desperate struggle. Every moment demanded their utmost focus as they juggled their resources: Mana, cooldown timers, and their rapidly fluctuating Health. Each second was a test of endurance, a battle to stay ahead of the meteor's cataclysmic assault.
Polly was still holding strong. But even she was beginning to falter.
"We can't hold this forever!" Broken shouted.
Freya had already shared detailed information in the Guild Chat about what Broken was doing and how everyone could contribute to absorbing the massive damage from the meteor.
Moments later, Tora took to the broadcast.
"Attention! This is critical-listen closely!" he announced. "Broken is fighting to stop the meteor, but he can't do it alone! The damage is too much for one person to handle!"
He thrust his hand into the air, his voice rising to a shout. "Raise your hands! We'll take on the meteor's damage together!"
On the ground, Max and others hesitated before following his lead, lifting their hands high. The action was almost instinctive.
"Ahhh!" Max screamed, yanking her hand back almost instantly.
"Tora, I can't! The damage is too much-my level's too low! I can't hold it!"
Tora's face tensed. He quickly lowered his own hand.

"Yes, Max!" he said, his voice urgent as he turned back to the broadcast. "Everyone, listen carefully! Cast any healing skills you have and stay close to your support teams! The damage is enormous-don't let yourselves die!"
Across the battlefield, voices erupted.
"Clerics, I need more healing over here!"
"I'm out of Mana potions! Someone, please cover me!"
"It's working, but it's draining me too fast!"
"Raise your hands! Don't let the damage fall back on them alone!"
"Healers, keep everyone alive! We need everyone at full strength!"
"Broken, you better win this for us!"
"KEEP CASTING! The meteor hasn't stopped moving!
"GO! Don't move, I'm healing you!"
"Damn it, we need more AoE heals-group up tighter!"
"DAMN THIS HEAT! Just how much longer can we hold?!"
[kenneth_burton]: "This is literally a Spirit Bomb moment. Where's Goku when you need
him?"
[McKenneth_Pearison]: "Tora's announcement: 'Share the damage!' Max: Shares damage
once and regrets every life decision."
[Sean_Weil]: "Tora out here like, 'IF YOU CAN HEAR MY VOICE, CLAP YOUR HANDS!' but
we're all dead inside."
[Corodix]: "Where's that guy who said 'it's just a game'? Come take 1% of this meteor damage
and THEN tell me that."
[Carl_Chalmers]: "Broken: activates everything. Meteor: 'Cool story, bro. Here's a fireball the
size of your hopes and dreams."
[DaoistLIML10]: "Raise your hands, they said. Takes 2 million damage. 'My therapist is gonna hear about this."
At the same time, across the battlefield, several figures surged into the air.
Elincia streaked upward, her body crackling with electricity as arcs of lightning danced around her.
Goldrich dashed across a series of floating platforms he summoned beneath his feet.
Nearby, a massive insect-like summon soared into view, piloted by Jovina.
Kingsley, in his Hawk Form, cut through the sky with powerful beats of his wings.
A wyvern rose next, ridden by Booba.
And finally, Tora spread his radiant wings. He turned back briefly to Max. "Max, I'm leaving the ground to you! Broken needs us in the sky!"
With that, he shot upward.

One by one, they converged around Broken, each casting their most defensive skills to contribute to the effort. But as soon as they drew close to the meteor's overwhelming heat and force, a chilling realization dawned upon them.
The sheer intensity of the damage began to drain their health at an alarming rate-faster than many of them had ever experienced.
Jovina gasped. "This is insane! My health's dropping just from being here!"
"Don't stop! We're here to back him up!"
"I didn't sign up for this level of madness. But... no turning back now!"

chapters.title: Chapter 696: All Hands to the Sky
paragraphs: "Damn it, we need more healers! I'll bring more healers from below!" Jovina shouted, her voice barely audible over the roaring flames. Her butterfly summon fluttered nearby, but it was doing little to lessen the damage they were all enduring together.
From below, a wyvern soared closer-it was Booba, with Starfall riding behind her.
"Oh, damn it, the damage is insane," Booba remarked as the wyvern circled around them.
Starfall wasted no time, casting an array of supportive skills, their effects barely holding as they all worked desperately to reinforce each other.
Earth shields, ice barriers, and countless other protective spells formed around them, only to melt or shatter almost instantly under the meteor's relentless assault.
"Where is the damn Trison?" Jovina yelled in frustration.
Elincia answered, her voice tight. "He was killed earlier."
"Damn it!" Jovina cursed. "When we need them most, they're gone!"

It was absolutely brutal. Everyone who had managed to gather around Broken was doing everything they could to survive. They threw every resource they had from their inventories- potions, rare consumables, and expensive scrolls-just to keep casting their skills and counteracting the relentless health drain that threatened to overwhelm them.

On the other hand, Broken, his usual calm demeanor slipping under the immense pressure, kept his eyes locked on his health bar. Despite its now higher health, it was draining faster than he'd ever seen, the rate of loss far outpacing any recovery efforts.
"More shields! More shields!" he shouted. Every second felt like a losing battle, the strain almost unbearable as the fiery destruction raged around them.

For the first time, true tension etched into his face. The responsibility of this colossal battle rested squarely on his shoulders. If he failed-if he fell-it would mean the end. Everything, everyone, would be lost.

A massive jolt shook the air around them, causing their positions to shift dangerously as the meteor pressed down with greater force. Panic rippled through the group as they struggled to maintain their position.
Broken's eyes darted to Polly, and he immediately realized the truth-she had reached her limit. Her wings faltered, her movements heavy and labored.
"Broken, you can release Polly," Goldrich called out. "I'll conjure a floating platform for us." "Polly, go," Broken said firmly. "You can't endure this any longer."

"Master... I-I can..." Polly's voice wavered, but her strength betrayed her. Her spirit energy was completely depleted, not giving her a choice. With one final flicker, her form shimmered and vanished, retreating back to the spirit world.

Now standing atop Goldrich's floating platform, Broken and Alora steadied themselves. But it was obvious that Goldrich, already taxed to his limits, could no longer cast as many protective shields as before. Their defenses were rapidly eroding under the relentless heat and pressure. Nearby, Tora hovered on his wings, but his abilities as an archer offered only minimal support to their dire situation. He turned back toward the camera broadcasting his message.
"We're all fighting together here!" he shouted. "Everyone on the ground, raise your hands high! We can't do this alone!

"The more of you who can make it up here to Broken's position, the less of the burden he'll have to carry alone! Every one of you counts-your strength, your skills, your presence. If you can fly or provide support, now is the time! Together, we can share this damage and keep fighting. Broken needs us, and this is our chance to make the difference!"

SexyBloom approached cautiously from below. However, she kept her distance, circling the battlefield. Occasionally, she retreated to avoid being overwhelmed, knowing the damage in Broken's vicinity could kill her instantly if she got too close without proper preparation.

Suddenly, a fast-spinning object shot up from below, spiraling wildly until it lost momentum near their position. All eyes turned toward the object as it slowed, and then, without warning, a familiar figure emerged.
"Ivana!" Jovina shouted. She quickly sent her butterfly summon to catch Ivana midair.

Ivana grabbed hold and gracefully leapt onto Goldrich's floating platform. Without hesitation, she slammed her shield onto its surface. Almost instantly, two massive protective shields formed around the group.

For the first time, Broken allowed himself a brief moment to glance at her. The shields she conjured were unlike anything they had seen before, and their immediate impact was undeniable-the strain on their defenses lessened significantly.
"Broken, how much longer do we need to hold this?" Jovina asked.
Before he could answer, Elincia spoke up. "From what I can see, there's a crack forming in the meteor. But I don't know... do we need to hold on until it completely breaks apart?"
"Damn it, this is insane," Jovina muttered. "I swear, I'm going to make whoever did this to us pay dearly."
The battlefield was still in chaos, far from under control. Some managed to raise their hands to offer support, but many couldn't withstand the overwhelming damage and fell.
Others formed parties with healers to share buffs and sustain themselves, but disorder persisted as surviving demons launched brutal attacks, undeterred by the meteor's destruction scorching them.
Broken and the others had made the right decision by unleashing massive area-of-effect attacks. Without that, the unchecked demons would have plunged the battlefield into even greater chaos.
"I can't do this! I'm out of Mana and health!"
"Damn it, even the meteor is burning us alive, and these bastards are still attacking!"
"Don't let the frontline collapse! Keep those demons back!"
"The damage is too much! I can't stay standing-someone help me!"
"Why aren't they retreating? They're burning up like we are, but they're still fighting!
"Keep fighting! We just need to buy time for Broken!"
"Don't give up! The kingdom is counting on us!"
Everyone was pushed to their absolute limit, burning through every resource they had. Expensive items for instant skill casts, potions, buffs-everything was being used to keep Broken alive.

It was clear they were now in a state of desperation. Whether they could succeed or not, none of them knew. All they could do was give their absolute best and hope it was enough. More and more players who could fly began to approach, each one maintaining just enough distance to avoid being completely overwhelmed by the intense heat and pressure. Ten, twenty-soon dozens of them were nearby, casting their support skills and buffs toward Broken and the others, doing everything they could to bolster the fragile defenses.
But the strain was relentless. Some lost their balance, their flight momentum failing as the scorching flames consumed them. Their screams echoed sharply as they plummeted toward
the ground.
One by one, others began to fall, the sheer intensity proving too much to endure.
Even Jovina, still desperately clinging to her resolve, grit her teeth in frustration. "Damn it," she growled. "My summon is running out of stamina. It's barely holding on!"
Until...
A figure shot upward, suddenly appearing near them. With a single powerful motion, he flapped his wings and crossed his arms.
All eyes turned toward him—a man draped in a green cloak, his long blonde hair flowing, and
a pair of wings that shimmered under the blazing light of the meteor.
"What a touching moment. Am I interrupting your little gathering?" the man said.
The group froze for a heartbeat, and then the tension rose sharply.
Rage and fear flared in equal measure. If the meteor wasn't already enough of an overwhelming threat, now they had to deal with him.
"Damn it," Jovina muttered. "As if things couldn't get worse."

chapters.title: Chapter 697: Cracks in the Sky, Cracks in Hope
paragraphs: It was Demian!

His form had changed slightly from before. Dark veins, like streams of blackened blood, spread across his skin, giving him a corrupted appearance. A pair of newly-formed wings unfurled from his back, carrying him upward as he closed the distance toward them with the group.
"Damn it, this bastard is really pushing my limits!" Jovina snapped.
"I'll take him on," Frostedge said firmly.
"No, Frostedge, let me handle this!" Elincia shouted back, her body crackling with blue energy as she separated from the group.
But before she could move, the wyvern that had been circling around suddenly dove with incredible speed toward Demian.
"Damn you, sucker! Now you're dealing with me!" Booba roared, slashing his sword as his wyvern charged at Demian.

Elincia followed quickly, unleashing a barrage of magic missiles that streaked toward him in rapid succession. The air around them erupted with rattling thunder, arcs of lightning crashing toward Demian with deafening force.

But Demian moved with infuriating grace, his wings beating powerfully as he dodged each attack effortlessly. The magic missiles and lightning slammed into the area around him, but The emerged unscathed.
Tora and the other nearby players took their shots at Demian, firing attacks in quick succession. But their efforts barely seemed to faze him.

With a single motion, Demian thrust his hand forward, unleashing a barrage of fast-moving magic missiles. One of them struck Tora directly, shattering his wings. "Tora!" someone screamed as he plummeted toward the ground below.

Demian pressed onward, effortlessly fending off the combined assaults of Booba and Elincia. When Booba's wyvern failed to land a hit, Demian retaliated mercilessly. A powerful magic missile struck the wyvern squarely, forcing it to dissipate back into its spirit form.
"Damn it, I'll be back, you fucker!"
Booba fell through the air, his scream echoing as he plunged downward.
"Booba! Damn it, where's all that arrogance you had earlier, huh?!"
Elincia continued her relentless assault, but without someone to tank for her, she became dangerously exposed.
Demian wasted no time, closing the distance between them with alarming speed.

Suddenly, a massive ice sword shot through the air, colliding with Demian mid-flight and forcing him back with an explosive impact. The force hurled Demian away from Elincia, buying her a critical moment to recover.
The ice sword was Frostedge's, but the maneuver cost him his balance. With no platform to stabilize himself, Frostedge tumbled toward the ground below, his figure disappearing from view.
The situation was rapidly deteriorating.

Just when it seemed the chaos couldn't escalate further, a thunderous flapping sound echoed from the distance. The air vibrated with the sheer force of the sound, followed by a deep, bone-chilling roar that reverberated across the battlefield.
From the shadows emerged a massive dragon-its skeletal frame glowing with a green aura.
Every eye turned toward the rider atop the skeletal dragon.
"It's... Galactron!" someone shouted in disbelief.
The skeletal dragon's jaws opened wide, and a colossal beam of energy, cannon-like in its intensity, blasted toward the struggling Demian.

Galactron unleashed dozens of magic circles high above the battlefield, each one glowing with a green light. From the circles, skeletal warriors rained down, each one charging toward Demian. They struck him with quick, single attacks before disintegrating into ash and vanishing.
Meanwhile, Galactron's massive skeletal dragon relentlessly pursued Demian, firing devastating beams of green energy in quick succession, each blast tearing through the air with terrifying force.
"What is that short idiot thinking?!" Jovina shouted in frustration.
Elincia, now back with the group, answered quickly, "It seems the rumors of betrayal within their ranks were true. This must have led to them turning on Demian."
"Looks like we have a common enemy," Goldrich added. "A temporary collaboration might not be such a bad idea."

Despite the unexpected backup, their situation continued to worsen. More of their allies had fallen to the ground, unable to withstand the unrelenting damage. Frostedge, too, was no longer with them after his fall, leaving their defenses even more strained.
"This is going to get even harder without Frostedge," Jovina muttered.

Elincia, however, shook her head slightly. "He's fallen from great heights before. I don't think he's easy to diel. Just like that necromancer over there." She motioned toward Galactron, who was orchestrating his skeletal army against Demian.
A deafening crack echoed through the air, followed by a massive roar as torrents of fire surged toward them from above.
"Damn it, I'm running out of resources," Goldrich muttered.
For someone like Goldrich, who was known for hoarding high-tier items and rare consumables, to say such a thing spoke volumes. This fight was bleeding them dry-both in strength and in wealth.

From the direction of Demian and Galactron, a sudden shift caught their attention. Demian's flight became erratic, his movements unsteady as he visibly took more and more damage. Then, without warning, he veered sharply and retreated into the darkness, vanishing from sight.
"Damn it, that bastard ran off!" Jovina shouted.
"I'm sure we'll still have to deal with him later," Goldrich said. "It looks like his transformation isn't finished yet."
"This should've been the perfect moment to kill him," Jovina snapped in response.

Their attention shifted again as the skeletal dragon flew toward them, circling slowly. Around them, countless magic circles began to appear. From each circle, skeletons emerged one after another, only to crumble into ash and flames moments later.
Still, this strange method of summoning provided crucial support, absorbing chunks of the meteor's relentless damage and easing the burden on Broken, even if only slightly.

Suddenly, another roar erupted. A massive crack, accompanied by an ear-splitting noise, spread across the meteor's surface. The blazing fire intensified, growing wilder and more uncontrollable as molten energy spilled outward.
Broken's eyes darted to his health bar, which was draining at an alarming rate. The speed of its decline far outpaced his healing capabilities, no matter how many buffs or skills he had active.
This can't hold much longer, he thought, his grip tightening.

Elincia's electric aura faded as her energy gave out, and she collapsed, falling from the sky. Jovina followed shortly after, her summons disappearing, leaving her to plummet helplessly toward the ground.
Before things could worsen, Frostedge suddenly reappeared. Without hesitation, he cast a massive ice barrier around the group.
But the reprieve didn't last.

A colossal explosion rocked the battlefield, the deafening sound shaking everything around them. The ice barrier shattered under the force, sending shards flying in all directions. The fiery blaze from the meteor grew even more intense, making the air almost impossible to breathe.
Broken staggered but forced himself to stay upright, gripping tightly to his resolve. Despite Frostedge's timely help, the danger had only escalated further.
The meteor finally reached its breaking point. A colossal explosion tore through the sky, shattering the air with a force so intense it seemed to freeze time for a heartbeat.

A deafening roar echoed across the battlefield as blinding light erupted from the meteor's surface, consuming everything in its vicinity with a fiery brilliance. The shockwave that followed rippled outward, tearing apart the clouds and shaking the very ground far below.

Flames exploded in chaotic waves, cascading like a volcanic eruption. Massive chunks of molten rock splintered away, hurling fiery debris in all directions. The blazing inferno painted the sky in hues of red and gold, as if the heavens themselves were on fire.

Above it all, the sound of the explosion was unrelenting-a constant, bone-shaking rumble that seemed to claw at their very cores. It wasn't just a sound-it was a force, one that vibrated through the air, the ground, and their bodies.
[The main threat has been destroyed.]
At that moment, the shattered meteor erupted in a cataclysmic explosion. Massive fragments of molten rock were sent hurtling in all directions, streaking across the sky like blazing comets.
Fiery shards slammed into the massive dome barrier surrounding the battlefield, each collision sending shockwaves rippling through its glowing structure. The dome trembled under the force.
Despite the destruction around them, a single thought united everyone: They had stopped the meteor, but the battle was far from over.
At the same time, the golden dome shattered, its protective glow breaking apart into countless fragments of light. The shield that had covered them was gone, leaving them exposed once more.

Above, large chunks of the meteor still remained, now falling rapidly toward the ground. Broken reached out instinctively, grabbing Alora's hand with one and Ivana's with the other as the three of them began to plummet together.

chapters.title: Chapter 698: The City in Ashes (Full-Length)
paragraphs: Broken plummeted freely through the chaos, the wind roaring past him as he desperately reached out. With his right hand, he caught Alora's, and with his left, he grabbed Ivana's. The three of them tumbled wildly through the air, their bodies spinning uncontrollably.

Explosions erupted all around them, the heat from the shattered meteor scorching their skin. Smaller fragments, even though still big enough, rained down alongside them, fiery shards from the once-massive meteor tumbling in every direction.
Yes, they had succeeded in destroying the largest threat-but the danger wasn't over. The smaller meteor fragments were still devastating.

Chunks of the meteor struck the city below, each impact creating massive explosions that sent shockwaves tearing through buildings. Fire and debris rippled outward, toppling entire blocks. The battlefield beyond the city was no safer-each piece that struck the ground caused massive damage, crushing demons and unfortunate combatants alike.

The destruction was relentless. Every impact brought a thunderous roar, shaking the earth and the sky. Smoke and fire spread in every direction as the ground erupted under the force of each collision.
Amidst the chaos, Broken and the two women continued to fall, the ground rushing closer with every second.
If they hit the ground from this height, there was no way they'd survive-not even with their strength. Broken had to think of something, fast.
His grip on Alora and Ivana tightened as he scanned the chaos below, searching for any way to break their fall.
Broken could use Moonlight Pocket Dimension to take himself and Alora to safety, but... Ivana? There was no way Broken would let Ivana fall to her death alone. He had to save them both.
As they fell, Ivana struggled to move closer, her voice barely audible over the roaring wind. "Broken! Take Princess Alora and go! I can handle myself!"
"No!"
"No!"
Broken and Alora shouted simultaneously.
Alora turned her gaze to Ivana. "If we combine every skill we have, maybe we can absorb the damage together."
"No, Princess! That's not an option," Ivana yelled. "You two go. It's the only way!"

But Broken's grip on Ivana's hand tightened. "No, Ivana. I won't leave you behind!" "Broken, it's better for me to take the fall than for all three of us to be lost!" Ivana insisted. "I said no!" Broken snapped.
Ivana hesitated, then said, "Let the Princess enter your pocket dimension. You stay here!"

But that plan wouldn't work either. Broken couldn't send Alora into the Moonlight Pocket Dimension alone-she could only enter if he accompanied her. There was no way around it, and time was running out.
"No one is being left behind!" Broken shouted.
He had to find another way.
Broken had no one to call for help. His allies were either caught in similar chaos or overwhelmed by the destruction below. There was no salvation in sight.
Until...
It appeared.

A massive figure shot toward them at incredible speed, striking them hard enough to send their bodies spinning uncontrollably. A powerful gust followed-accompanied by the unmistakable shadow of a massive skeletal dragon.

The dragon's enormous jaws snapped shut around the three of them, but instead of crushing them, a green aura enveloped their bodies. They floated within its maw, suspended and protected by the strange, shimmering energy.
Galactron!
The skeletal dragon wasn't harming them-it had come to save them.

Inside the glowing green space, their movements stabilized, and the relentless pull of gravity eased. But outside, chaos still raged. Another fiery boulder slammed into the dragon, this time from the side, forcing it into a brutal roll mid-flight. They were thrown around again inside the glowing green energy, but the dragon continued to fight against the chaos.

The three of them stood together, their eyes fixed on the city and battlefield ahead. The remnants of the meteor still rained down, streaking fire across the sky. The once-beautiful city, with its glowing lights illuminating the night, now burned under the assault, flames consuming what had been a symbol of life and hope.

chapters.title: Chapter 699: The Burning Eye of the End (Full-Length)
paragraphs: The massive magic circle floating high above was eerily similar to the one that had summoned the meteor earlier. Its glow cast an oppressive light over the city and the battlefield, stretching across the horizon.

It was a sight that made hearts feel as if they had stopped beating, an oppressive weight pulling at their very souls. The sheer magnitude of it, paired with the lingering destruction below, seemed to snuff out any remaining hope.
What about the city's remaining inhabitants? Were there any survivors left, or had the destruction claimed them all?

On the battlefield, the panic was so real, though it felt different now-less frantic, more drained. People moved sluggishly, their energy spent, their spirits shattered. Some didn't even react to the looming threat, perhaps too exhausted to muster fear.

Broken directed Beebot to keep moving, the crawling carriage skimming over rubble and destruction as he searched for the rest of his companions. They reached the West Gate, where a figure sprinted toward them from a distance. As the figure came closer, it stopped directly in front of the carriage, blocking its path.
It was Fokil.
The blacksmith dwarf stood firm, his gaze meeting Broken's. Without hesitation, Ivana jumped down from the carriage and ran to him, wrapping her arms around him tightly. "You survived," Fokil said.
"Mr. Fokil, I'm so glad you're alive too," Ivana replied.
Broken approached the dwarf, who turned to look at him.
"You did well, kid," Fokil said.
"Thanks, sir," Broken offered a weary smile and nodded back, the weight of everything still pressing heavily on his shoulders.
One by one, more familiar faces began to appear. Optimus arrived first, followed by Elincia, who soared toward them with her crackling blue aura flickering faintly. She was battered but alive.

Then came Kingsley, Goldrich, Jovina, Starfall, Charmelyn, Skywarden, Booba, and even Frostedge. All of them converged at the same point, gathering together. They were bruised, battered, and exhausted-but they were alive.
As the group caught their breath, their eyes instinctively turned upward, drawn again to the massive magic circle above.
No one spoke. The only sounds were the distant cries of demons running wild, players shouting for their companions, and the faint rumble of collapsing structures. Chaos reigned all around them.
And then...
The magic circle began to shift. Its patterns glowed even brighter, twisting and contorting as though something massive was forcing its way through.
The glowing lines split apart - deliberately cleaved the magic circle in two.
The halves pulled away, revealing something far more terrifying than anyone could have imagined.
A massive, singular eye.

It burned with a fire, its gaze seemingly piercing through the entire battlefield and the city below. For a moment, no one moved, no one spoke. They were frozen in fear, their minds unable to process the sheer horror of what they were seeing.
[In the presence of the King, the supreme ruler of Hell, all must bow.]

The notification appeared, but its weight was more than just words. All across the battlefield, the demons fell to their knees in unison, bowing to the enormous eye as if compelled by an invisible force.
[Anyone below Level 300 will have their weight capacity increased by 90% of their total capacity.]
Suddenly, players and NPCs alike crumpled to the ground, struggling under an unbearable weight that seemed to drag them down.
[Anyone below Level 300 will experience a 30% reduction in stats.]
[Anyone below Level 300 will take damage over time: 2% of Health per second.]

The notifications continued to pour in, each one striking like a hammer. Those who had managed to stay on their feet moments ago now fell, clutching at the ground as if trying to resist an invisible force pressing them down.
Cries of despair filled the air:
"What... What is this? I can't move!"
"It's too heavy! I... I can't even breathe!"
"Our stats... they're gone! I feel so weak!" "How do we fight something like this?!"
"I... I can't do this anymore. This is impossible!
"We barely survived the meteor, and now this?!"

Around them, hope seemed to drain from the battlefield like water spilling from a cracked vessel. Faces were pale, bodies trembling under the crushing weight. Even those who had been so determined moments ago now wore expressions of dread and defeat.
[Elincia]: "Is that... King Bael?"
[Freya]: "Judging by how he refers to himself, it's most likely King Bael, the ranked number one named demon. The wielder of the Gluttony Champion."
[Booba]: "Damn it, could this get any worse?"
[Goldrich]: "Looking at how he's only showing his eye, it seems like he can't fully manifest here. That's probably as far as he can go."
[Jovina]: "What the hell are you saying, old man?"

[Freya]: "I think the meteor Demian tried to drop earlier was likely part of a ritual. With that meteor, it's clear he doesn't want the Dissidia Kingdom for himself. He wants to destroy it." [Booba]: "That bastard. I feel like tearing his eye out of its socket myself."
[Freya]: "If Demian's goal with the meteor was to kill the people of Dissidia, then it's
possible they were meant as sacrifices for a kind of ritual."
[Goldrich]: "So the ritual failed, and now King Bael is furious, stuck peeking at us from Hell?
Khi khi khi."
[Jovina]: "Why are you laughing in a situation like this, old man?!"
The massive eye blinked slowly.
The battlefield fell into an eerie silence, broken only by the faint crackle of flames and the labored breaths of those struggling to move under the overwhelming weight.
And then, a voice.
Deep, resonant, and impossibly vast, it filled the space, as if the very heavens were speaking.
But surprisingly, it was calm, and measured.
"Your struggles, your defiance... how pitifully small they appear before me."
The eye narrowed slightly, its gaze sweeping across the battlefield.

"This place, this kingdom, this fragile cradle of fleeting ambition-it was doomed the moment it came into existence. Its light, its hope, its people... all of it, a mere spark waiting to be extinguished."
The voice grew colder.
"I do not destroy out of anger or whim. No... this is inevitability. Your existence is a flaw, a stain upon the grand design. And so, I will purge it, as easily as snuffing out a candle."
A flicker of fire blazed within the eye.
"Look around you. Your allies, your friends... Do you feel the cracks forming? The bonds breaking? You fight, you endure, but for what? To delay the inevitable? How fragile you are.
How weak."
The magic circle above began to twist and pulse. The sky itself seemed to darken further, consumed by the shadow of the massive presence before them.
"Yunatea will fall. Your defiance amuses me, but it will not change the outcome. The weight of my will is absolute, and you... are nothing."
The battlefield trembled under the force of his words, and despair seeped deeper into the hearts of those who heard them.
[Chase406]: "Bro is literally monologuing like a Shakespearean villain. Someone throw a
tomato!
[bloodthorn]: "'You are nothing.' Bruh, we KNOW. No need to rub it in!"
[Shadow_Monarch_48]: "'Purge the world'-cool story, dude. Can you let us finish lunch
first?"
[Marvin_Delawder]: "Can we all agree we are NOT logging in tomorrow? Like, let's just
pretend this didn't happen."
[b_duty]: "Petition to ban whoever thought summoning an eye the size of a city was good
game design."
[Baffen]: "Bold of him to assume we haven't already given up emotionally."
[bukli_ajrullai]: "Raise your hand if you also feel like a 'flaw' in the grand design. Just me?"
[dan_greany]: "Did he just say 'snuff us out like a candle'? At least he's poetic about our
deaths."
[Claire_D_7176]: "Okay, team meeting-who's got an idea for surviving this? No? Cool,
cool."

The battlefield was frozen, not just by fear but by the sheer weight of uncertainty. What was everyone doing? Waiting? Hoping this was some kind of nightmare? Or was this just another overly dramatic monologue from the supposed main villain of this grand game? Surely the King-the Supreme Ruler of Hell-wasn't planning to descend now, right? It was too soon for something like this. This couldn't possibly be the endgame.
The game was only three years old! The developers clearly wanted to keep making money, so why throw the ultimate villain into the mix this early?
Why now?
Why?!

Damn it, there were still plenty of people who just wanted to have fun playing this game. Not everyone signed up for battles like this! This war had dragged on too long already. People's resources were drained. Their spirits were spent. The battlefield wasn't full of warriors ready to fight-it was full of players silently begging for it all to end.
Someone-anyone-please, end this war!
That was the overwhelming thought shared by the majority of players and NPCs alike.
And then...
It appeared.
A massive, no, but super massive palm-ethereal and made entirely of flame-materialized in the air above them. Its sheer size was incomprehensible, blotting out the already dimmed sky.
And then it fell.

The palm descended toward the earth with a terrifying speed, like a god swatting an insect from the ground. The air crackled with unbearable heat, and the weight of it pressed against everyone's chests, forcing them to their knees.
"Hell... this is the end."
"Fuck this, I'm out!" "What do we do?! What CAN we do?!"
"Run? Hide? It doesn't matter! We're done!"
"Someone... anyone... stop this!"
Panic spread, but it was too late. The flaming palm came crashing down, and for a moment, it felt like everything-everything-was about to end.

The eye narrowed slightly, its gaze sweeping across the battlefield.
"This place, this kingdom, this fragile cradle of fleeting ambition-it was doomed the moment it came into existence.
Its light, its hope, its people... all of it, a mere spark waiting to be extinguished."
The voice grew colder.
"I do not destroy out of anger or whim.
No... this is inevitability.
Your existence is a flaw, a stain upon the grand design.
And so, I will purge it, as easily as snuffing out a candle."
A flicker of fire blazed within the eye.
"Look around you.
Your allies, your friends...
Do you feel the cracks forming?
The bonds breaking?
You fight, you endure, but for what?
To delay the inevitable?
How fragile you are.
How weak."
The magic circle above began to twist and pulse.
The sky itself seemed to darken further, consumed by the shadow of the massive presence before them.
"Yunatea will fall.
Your defiance amuses me, but it will not change the outcome.
The weight of my will is absolute, and you... are nothing."
The battlefield trembled under the force of his words, and despair seeped deeper into the hearts of those who heard them.

No need to rub it in!"

Can you let us finish lunch
first?"

pretend this didn't happen."

game design."

deaths."

No?
Cool,
cool."
The battlefield was frozen, not just by fear but by the sheer weight of uncertainty.
What was everyone doing?
Waiting?
Hoping this was some kind of nightmare?
Or was this just another overly dramatic monologue from the supposed main villain of this grand game?
Surely the King-the Supreme Ruler of Hell-wasn't planning to descend now, right?
It was too soon for something like this.
This couldn't possibly be the endgame.
The game was only three years old!
The developers clearly wanted to keep making money, so why throw the ultimate villain into the mix this early?
Why now?
Why?!
Damn it, there were still plenty of people who just wanted to have fun playing this game.
Not everyone signed up for battles like this!
This war had dragged on too long already.
People's resources were drained.
Their spirits were spent.
The battlefield wasn't full of warriors ready to fight-it was full of players silently begging for it all to end.
Someone-anyone-please, end this war!
That was the overwhelming thought shared by the majority of players and NPCs alike.
And then...
It appeared.
A massive, no, but super massive palm-ethereal and made entirely of flame-materialized in the air above them.
Its sheer size was incomprehensible, blotting out the already dimmed sky.
And then it fell.
The palm descended toward the earth with a terrifying speed, like a god swatting an insect from the ground.
The air crackled with unbearable heat, and the weight of it pressed against everyone's chests, forcing them to their knees.
"Hell... this is the end."
"Fuck this, I'm out!" "What do we do?!
What CAN we do?!"
"Run?
Hide?
It doesn't matter!
We're done!"
"Someone... anyone... stop this!"
Panic spread, but it was too late.
The flaming palm came crashing down, and for a moment, it felt like everything-everything-was about to end.

chapters.title: Chapter 700 - The Silence After the Storm?
paragraphs: The giant flame-shaped palm shot downward, blazing fast and unstoppable. No one could move. Everyone was pinned to the ground, trapped under its crushing pressure.
And then, it hit.
People braced for the worst, shutting their eyes in fear. But instead of destruction, there was nothing.
Just an eerie, stunned silence.
Slowly, people began to look around, their expressions filled with confusion. No one was hurt. No one was burning. The crushing weight that had pinned them moments ago was suddenly... gone.
The debuff had also been lifted.
"Damn? Seriously?"
"Where is the damage?"
"This is quite surprising, and unexpected..."

All heads turned back toward the sky, where the massive magic circle that had filled the heavens was now dimming. The flames that once burned within its patterns flickered weakly before crumbling into ash and disappearing completely.
The sky returned to its normal, dark night, leaving only the fires from the meteor fragments and the wreckage of the city below to light the battlefield.
The massive, unrelenting eye was gone, vanished without a trace.
"Seriously?" another voice said. "When we thought this was the end of everything?"
It seemed as though the catastrophe had passed. For now, at least. The crushing pressure was gone, and everyone could move again as if nothing had happened.
[Goldrich]: "I knew it. The King was only peeking out from Hell to give Yunatea a little 'hello.'"
[Booba]: "Yeah, but don't get too comfortable. We've still got a job to do—take care of those damn demons."
[Jovina]: "Let's go kill them all and end this tiring night!"
The battlefield stirred once more as the reality of the ongoing fight sank in. The threat wasn't entirely over. There was still a battle to win.
The roars of demons echoed once more across the battlefield, a grim reminder that the war was not over yet.
But... no more named demons, right? And the remaining forces? They weren't as overwhelming as before. This wasn't impossible. They could win this.

Broken sprinted toward the spot where his Bedrock Breaker still lay embedded in the ground. No one had dared to lay a finger on it—Freya had made sure of that. She had coordinated with a few guilds, ensuring their members were stationed nearby to guard the weapon until its rightful owner came back.
Gripping the pickaxe firmly, Broken immediately dashed forward.
Whatever comes next, the enemy must be eliminated now.

The battlefield roared back to life as defenders scattered, heading to their designated posts. The gates were still under attack, each one a critical point that needed protection. The fight wasn't over, and every part of the city demanded their attention.

Broken surged ahead. His Bedrock Breaker glinted under the flames of battle as he swung it with precision. With one fluid motion, he brought it down in an overhead strike, cleaving through a demon with ease. The creature disintegrated into ash.
His actions didn't go unnoticed. Others on the battlefield saw him charging ahead. Cries of hope and resolve erupted from all directions.
"Let's go! This isn't over!"
"Support me, now!"
"I'll give it everything I've got!"
"We're so close to victory! Let's finish this!"
The battlefield came alive with energy, the once-crippling despair now replaced by a fiery determination to win.
They had survived against all odds—four named demons, a colossal meteor that nearly obliterated the city, and even the oppressive presence of Hell's supposed ruler. They had endured it all.
And now, as the fires of the battlefield roared and the shouts of allies echoed through the chaos, one thing was clear.
The fight wasn't over yet!

The battle dragged on for several minutes, each second feeling like an eternity. Everyone on the battlefield used up what little resources they had left, fighting with sheer determination and desperation. Despite their exhaustion, they pushed forward relentlessly, slowly but surely reducing the number of demons.
Reinforcements began to arrive from the gates—players who, inspired by the glimmers of hope, joined the fray to clear out the remaining enemies. Their combined efforts began to turn the tide.
Broken, shifted to another gate to retrieve his remaining weapons. The momentum of the battle continued to build, and within minutes, the fight began to stabilize.
The West, East, South, and North gates all saw a drastic reduction in demon numbers. The tide of the battle was turning, with demons falling one by one, their forces diminishing rapidly.

As the end drew nearer, Broken used his Bedrock Breaker one final time. Slamming it into the earth, he unleashed a massive earthquake that tore through the battlefield. The ground split and trembled, sending massive boulders crashing down from heaven. The impact obliterated dozens of demons in an instant, scattering their ashes into the air.

The final blow came with a decisive strike against the last demon in his path. His weapon cleaved through the creature, and as its body dissolved into nothingness, silence began to settle over the battlefield.
Broken surveyed the area around him. The demons that remained were scattered and vastly outnumbered. It was clear that the remaining defenders could handle the cleanup.
Turning his gaze, he spotted Alora in the distance. She had just finished her own battle, her weapon lowered as she caught her breath.
Broken sprinted toward Alora, with Ivana quickly joining them.
"This area is clear," Alora said.
"Yes, and—" Broken began, but Alora cut in.
"We need to find out who's still alive in the city," she said firmly.

Broken nodded. Even in the chaos and devastation, with no clear leadership in the kingdom, the royal knights and troops were still dedicated to their duties. Without needing orders, they spread out across the city, aiding survivors and evacuating those who needed help.
In some areas, the atmosphere shifted. Cries of victory began to ripple through the ruins. Warriors, exhausted and battered, dropped to the ground, overcome by relief.
"We did it... we survived!"
"The demons are gone! It's finally over!"
"I can't believe it... we actually won."
"Thank the gods... we're still here."
"Someone get me a drink, I'm not moving for a week!"
"We fought Hell itself, and we're still standing!"
"This city... it's broken, but it's ours! We'll rebuild it together."

As the battlefield quieted, it was officially confirmed—the demons in the city and beyond its walls had all been defeated. A triumphant cheer rose from the surviving defenders, echoing across the ruined city.
The victory was hard-fought, and the sound of celebration carried with it both relief and exhaustion.

The royal knights and kingdom troops wasted no time, shifting their focus to evacuating the surviving citizens. Carriages rolled into the city in long, orderly lines, and the remaining civilians were carefully escorted onto them.
The evacuation was a necessary precaution—not only because the city lay in ruins and required extensive repairs, but also to prepare for any potential unforeseen threats that might arise.
"I thought this was the end... but look at us—we made it!"
"But man, are you sure this is really over? I still can't wrap my head around it," someone said with a nervous laugh.
"Haha... it just feels like the kind of nightmare that doesn't end, you know?"
Others nearby nodded, some offering faint smiles, others still scanning the sky as if expecting another disaster to strike. The relief was real, but the lingering unease was hard to shake.
